To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the positive effects of FDI on innovation system capabilities are contingent upon the level of systemic absorbative capacities.
FDI’s effects on developing countries’ innovation capabilities are mediated by the level of systemic absorbtive capacities, and that these contributions are not pervasive.

(i) FDI has positive effects on productivity in developing countries, (ii) FDI has stronger effects in countries with better systemic absorptive capacities, and (iii) FDI effects are not pervasive, as it is only positively associated with labor productivity gains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mediating role that systemic absorptive capacity plays between FDI and the innovation system’s overall capabilities.
the identification of the role played by FDI in developing countries’ National Innovation Systems.
the mediating effects that innovation policy can have in the relationship between FDI and innovation system performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FDI effects in innovation systems of developing countries are not pervasive and are not necessarily positive.
FDI’s contributions to innovation system development are not automatic.
the positive effects of FDI are not a given, and that the role of the innovation system is determinant in this regard.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the effects of FDI on innovation are not as significant as expected.
FDI effects are contingent upon the existent innovation policy framework.
FDI’s effects are mediated by systemic absorptive capacities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the role of FDI in developing countries’ National Innovation Systems is not straightforward and that its positive effects are not automatic, but rather dependent upon the existent level and the evolution of systemic absorptive capabilities in these countries.
, although FDI can be a strategic tool to promote economic development in developing countries, its effects are not automatic, and that it should be complemented with systemic initiatives.
FDI’s effects in developing countries are contingent upon the existent levels of systemic absorptive capabilities.
